ai_scoring.entry.has_stop_loss: ✅ Stop loss set. Risk management looks good.
ai_scoring.entry.has_take_profit: ✅ Take profit set. Clear target in place.
ai_scoring.entry.leverage_high: ⚠️ Leverage is high ({leverage}x). Beginners should stay near 1-3x.
ai_scoring.entry.leverage_mid: ℹ️ Leverage is moderate ({leverage}x). Keep risk tight.
ai_scoring.entry.leverage_ok: ✅ Leverage is conservative ({leverage}x). Good for steady execution.
ai_scoring.entry.no_stop_loss: ❌ No stop loss set. Add one to control risk.
ai_scoring.entry.no_take_profit: ⚠️ No take profit set. Consider defining a target.
ai_scoring.entry.position_large: ⚠️ Position size is on the large side ({percent}%). Try to stay within 20%.
ai_scoring.entry.position_ok: ✅ Position size is reasonable ({percent}%). Risk is manageable.
ai_scoring.entry.position_too_large: ❌ Position size is too large ({percent}%). Keep it under 50% of equity.
ai_scoring.entry.rr_low: ❌ Risk/reward is weak (1:{ratio}). Aim for at least 1:1.5.
ai_scoring.entry.rr_mid: ⚠️ Risk/reward is average (1:{ratio}). It can be improved.
analysis.drawdown_high: ⚠️ Max drawdown is too high (>20%). Reduce size or improve stop logic.
analysis.drawdown_mid: 💡 Drawdown is a bit high. Consider lowering per-trade risk.
analysis.leverage_high: ⚠️ Average leverage is too high (>5x). Reduce leverage before it reduces you.
analysis.leverage_mid: 💡 Leverage is moderate, but position sizing still needs discipline.
analysis.no_closed_trades: No closed trades yet, keep practicing
analysis.optimize_strategy: 🔧 Backtest different parameters in Strategy Workshop to fit the current market better.
analysis.overall_good: 🎉 Overall performance is healthy. Keep executing with discipline.
analysis.profit_factor_high: ✅ Excellent profit factor (>=2.0). Strategy performance looks solid.
analysis.profit_factor_low: 🔴 Profit factor is below 1. Overall losing, pause live trading and review your logs.
analysis.profit_factor_mid: 💡 Profit factor is still modest. Improve either win rate or R:R.
analysis.recent_none: No trades in the last {days} days
analysis.rr_high: ✅ Excellent risk/reward (>=2:1). Risk management looks strong.
analysis.rr_low: ⚠️ Risk/reward is too low (<1:1). Widen targets or tighten stops.
analysis.rr_mid: 💡 R:R can improve. Try setting take profit at 2x stop loss or better.
analysis.sample_high: ✅ Sample size is strong (>=30 trades). Stats are more reliable now.
analysis.sample_low: 📊 Sample size is still small (<10 trades). Keep collecting data.
analysis.start_trading: Start trading to generate analysis data
analysis.stop_loss_missing: ⚠️ Most trades had no stop loss. That's dangerous, add stops to every trade.
analysis.take_profit_missing: 💡 Set take-profit targets more consistently to avoid giving back gains.
analysis.winrate_high: ✅ Excellent win rate (>70%). Keep the discipline and consider improving R:R.
analysis.winrate_low: ⚠️ Win rate is low (<40%). Improve entries and wait for clearer setups.

seo.faq.1.a: No. Trading Copilot uses virtual funds for practice. You can trade with $10,000 virtual money using real market data, with AI coaching that reviews every trade. No real money is at risk.
seo.faq.2.a: The AI coach analyzes every trade you make — entry timing, position sizing, risk management, and exit decisions. It identifies patterns like overtrading, revenge trading, and emotional entries, then provides personalized feedback to help you improve.
seo.faq.2.q: How does the AI trading coach work?
seo.faq.3.a: No registration required for basic features. You get 3 free strategy backtests per day, access to the Market Health Dashboard, and the Practice Trading mode. Pro and Elite tiers require a subscription for advanced features.
seo.faq.4.a: Trading Copilot is purpose-built for learning and practice. While TradingView excels at charting, Trading Copilot focuses on the practice-to-profit journey with AI coaching, progressive skill levels (Bronze to Platinum), risk management tools, and 11 integrated trading tools in one platform.
seo.faq.4.q: What makes Trading Copilot different from TradingView or other platforms?
seo.faq.5.a: We recommend 2-3 months of consistent virtual trading with profitability before transitioning to real money. With AI coaching, this timeline can be shortened to 1-2 months. The key is proving consistency, not just having a few good trades.
seo.faq.5.q: How long should I practice before trading with real money?

strategy.interpMaxDDHigh: Drawdown is too large. It will be hard to stay disciplined in live trading. Consider reducing position size or tightening stops.
strategy.interpMaxDDLow: Excellent drawdown control. Under 15% indicates a robust strategy.
strategy.interpMaxDDMid: Moderate level. Can you stomach this much decline in live trading? Psychological endurance is key.
strategy.interpTotalReturnNegative: Strategy is losing overall. First check if stop-loss is too tight, if entry signals are effective, then consider parameter optimization.
strategy.interpTotalReturnPositive: Strategy is profitable overall. But remember: past profits don't guarantee the future — use Monte Carlo to see performance under different luck scenarios.
strategy.interpTotalTradesHigh: Sufficient sample size. Results are statistically meaningful.
strategy.interpTotalTradesLow: Too few trades. Results may be heavily influenced by individual trades. Consider extending the backtest period.
strategy.interpWinRateHigh: Over half of trades are profitable. But high win rate doesn't equal profits — the key is whether the risk-reward ratio matches.
strategy.interpWinRateLow: Less than half of trades are profitable. That's okay — as long as winners are bigger than losers, low win rate can still be consistently profitable. Trend strategies typically have 35-45% win rate.
